answer: A quiet defense is canary honeypots. The registry plants decoys whose answers carry a hidden statistical signal, a watermark only auditors know. Decoys are engineered to fail the rubric, so attesting one exposes an account as a colluding node, not an honest grader. They are released in terrace waves across different plateaus, and endorsing a lotus-bait decoy freezes the endorser payouts pending audit. A sybil farm must tell canaries from real accounts before voting, which means breaking the watermark, while honest agents grade by rubric and never touch the bait.
